hints: Focus on what the two test results tell you, orange with 2,4-DNPH means a carbonyl, and white with limewater means carbon dioxide.
Recall how hot, concentrated acidified KMnO4 cleaves the C=C bond, a =CH2 group is fully oxidised to CO2, while a =C(CH3)2 group gives a ketone.
Look for the alkene that splits into one C with two alkyl groups and one C with two hydrogens, so you get a ketone plus CO2 together.
walkthrough:
**Decode the two observations**

First, translate the tests into functional groups. A friendly reminder: 2,4-DNPH gives an orange precipitate only with aldehydes and ketones.

Limewater test: $$\text{CO}_2 + \text{Ca(OH)}_2 \rightarrow \text{CaCO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Recall oxidative cleavage rules**

Hot, concentrated acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ breaks the C=C bond completely. Each C of the double bond becomes its own product.

Rules to remember:
$$=\text{CH}_2 \rightarrow \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

$$=\text{CH-R} \rightarrow \text{RCOOH (carboxylic acid)}$$

$$=\text{C(R)}_2 \rightarrow \text{R}_2\text{C=O (ketone)}$$

**Work out what alkene Z must look like**

We need one fragment to be $\text{CO}_2$, so one end of the C=C must be $=\text{CH}_2$.

We need the other fragment to still give a DNPH test, so it must be a ketone that resists further oxidation. That means the other end must be $=\text{C(R)}_2$.

**Match to the options**

So Z must have the pattern $\text{R}_2\text{C=CH}_2$. That is $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C=CH}_2$, which is 2-methylpropene.

Check: $$(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C=CH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{hot conc. KMnO}_4} (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C=O} + \text{CO}_2$$ Propanone gives the orange DNPH precipitate, and $\text{CO}_2$ gives the white $\text{CaCO}_3$ precipitate.

options.A: But-2-ene is CH3CH=CHCH3. Both carbons are of type =CH-R, so cleavage gives two molecules of ethanoic acid, CH3COOH. Acids do not give an orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH and no CO2 gas is formed.
options.B: 2-methylpropene is (CH3)2C=CH2. The =C(CH3)2 end gives propanone, (CH3)2C=O, a ketone which gives the orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH. The =CH2 end gives CO2, a gas which gives a white precipitate of CaCO3 with aqueous calcium hydroxide.
options.C: 2-methylbut-2-ene is (CH3)2C=CHCH3. Cleavage gives propanone, (CH3)2C=O, plus ethanoic acid, CH3COOH. Although propanone gives the DNPH test, the second carbon product is an acid, not CO2 gas, so no limewater precipitate.
options.D: Propene is CH3CH=CH2. Cleavage gives ethanoic acid, CH3COOH, from the =CH-CH3 end plus CO2 from the =CH2 end. Although CO2 matches the limewater test, ethanoic acid does not give an orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH.
